data.name: Aurelia banked memory organization
data.description: AION system controller combines DMA, 4 KiB bank mapping and CPU-independent system-DRAM refresh. Dedicated sprite SRAM is accessed through video upload ports.

specification.common_ram_budget_status: Initial planning allocation; validate against firmware, buffers and interrupt requirements.
specification.implementation: One AION system-controller chip replaces mapper registers and selected decode/control logic; external clock/reset/interrupt and electrical buffers remain as required.
specification.rom_policy: Read-only code and constants execute directly from ROM where practical. Mutable state, stacks and buffers reside in RAM.
specification.video_ram_policy: CPU uses temporary 4 KiB display-memory windows or auto-incrementing upload ports. DMA uses physical source banks and target-ready video ports. Video controller independently refreshes display DRAM and arbitrates sprite SRAM; sprite storage is not system RAM.
specification.reset_policy: Initialize refresh and boot mapping before RAM use; disable DMA and clear pending ownership on reset. Warm boot aborts/drains DMA before restoring bank maps.
specification.application_policy: Installed RAM is accessible, but system workspaces and the resident Business Tools workspace reduce application memory.
specification.expansion_policy: Additional RAM uses mapped pages; an expansion does not enlarge the CPU logical address space.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: CP/M-compatible application-memory boundary
implementation_design.discovery: At launch, the little-endian word at 0006H (the operand of JMP at 0005H) points to the BDOS entry stub at the exclusive top of usable contiguous application RAM. Keep the entire advertised range writable RAM.
implementation_design.budget: Reserve 4 KB at the top of lower RAM for the entry stub and resident workspace, in addition to F000–FFFF common system RAM. These are the initial design allocations, not measured image sizes. If implementation requires more workspace, revise the boot profile before application launch and report the actual lower boundary.
dispatch: The stub jumps to common memory before any bank mapping changes.
Common code saves mapping and application stack, then adopts the system stack.
Map the service; copy caller buffers in bounded chunks while respecting page boundaries.
Restore the application view and stack before returning.
lifecycle: Choose all workspace reservations before launching the program. Never shrink TPA under a running program.
Warm boot restores vectors and the normal map. Legacy programs with hardcoded addresses beyond the published boundary remain unsupported.
Disable optional resident tools or choose a smaller TPA when networking needs more RAM; never silently consume advertised program memory.
implementation_design.extension_api: lx_memory_query returns installed RAM, TPA bounds, reserved bytes and optional banked-handle capacity. Standard CP/M programs need not use it.
validation: Exercise programs that inspect 0006H and fill their advertised TPA.
Test nested calls, interrupts, DMA buffers crossing pages and warm boot after application failure.
Stress CPU/DMA/refresh/peripherals and display together at both host clocks and process/temperature corners.
Validate hidden and expanded RAM refresh, physical DMA bounds, page-crossing segmentation, abort and warm boot.

application_memory_profiles.status: Specified initial allocation; any future budget change must preserve the published boundary for each running program.

dma.bank_selection: Latch physical source/destination bank and offsets on start. CPU mapping changes cannot redirect an active transfer; split logical buffers at 4 KiB boundaries before programming physical segments. Reject ROM writes, unmapped banks and out-of-range lengths.
dma.arbitration: Bounded bursts with guaranteed CPU and refresh service; device-ready/WAIT handshake; video uploads yield to video-controller fetch deadlines. Numeric grant limits require cycle-level validation.
dma.completion: Completion/error interrupt, readable remaining count, controlled abort; reset disables DMA.
dma.video_endpoint: Auto-incrementing upload ports for display DRAM or dedicated sprite SRAM; target-ready backpressure.
dma.peripheral_scope: Disk/FlexiBUS DMA requires qualified request/ready or FIFO endpoints and drivers; legacy programmed I/O remains supported.

system_refresh.scope: System DRAM only, including hidden banks and expansion. Video controller refreshes display DRAM; sprite SRAM needs no refresh.
system_refresh.scheduler: Always-running timer, row counter and refresh arbitration during CPU execution, HALT and DMA; initialize before enabling RAM use. Match row count and retention deadlines to each qualified system DRAM type.
supported_populations: 48 KiB: three banks of eight 16Kx1 DRAMs
64 KiB expanded Aurelia: four banks of eight 16Kx1 DRAMs
64 KiB Aurelia+: one bank of eight 64Kx1 DRAMs

regions.description: Includes page zero and the lower application area.
Remaining application RAM, motherboard ROM, cartridge ROM or video RAM, selected in 4 KB pages.
Stable entry routines, system stack, critical interrupt code and mutable system state.

call_sequence: Enter a stable routine in common memory.
Save application mapping and stack; switch to the system stack.
Map the required ROM and data/video RAM pages.
Execute the service; use a common buffer or alternate window for hidden application data.
Restore mapping and stack, then return.
requirements: Preserve interrupt safety across every permitted mapping.
Separate writable state from ROM code and remove or relocate self-modifying code.
Final ROM capacities, timing and common-memory budget require implementation validation.
Qualify CPU bus handover at 4 and 6 MHz, bounded DMA bursts, device-ready waits, completion interrupts and abort/reset recovery.
Verify independent refresh for every installed physical bank, including hidden banks and Aurelia 16 KiB expansion; derive deadlines from qualified DRAM ordering codes.
Freeze package/pinout, external buffers, memory decode, bank-latched DMA addressing and simultaneous video/peripheral stress tests.
data.normal_map_explanation: Normal mapping describes what the CPU sees while an application runs. Mapper capability describes which addresses can change. The same 7000–EFFF switching capability exists in every configuration, even when those addresses normally contain RAM.
data.full_ram_explanation: With 64 KB installed (Aurelia+ or expanded Aurelia), 0000–EFFF contains 60 KB lower RAM and F000–FFFF contains 4 KB common system RAM. B000–EFFF is therefore RAM rather than a permanently reserved ROM window. System calls temporarily overlay selected pages with ROM/cartridge/video RAM, then restore RAM. The Z80 never sees all physical RAM and ROM simultaneously.
